attribution.note: Zitron's own words, written in the first person in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'I believe ... will have to' states a firm expectation, not a hedge, so this is a scored forecast. The either/or (raise prices or begin to collapse), the open 'like' set of companies and the 'at some point' horizon are all kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: a broad, cost-driven price rise for comparable service, or clear financial failure. Counting new-tier or capability-justified price rises only as weak evidence matches the speaker's cost-pressure argument.

evidence.note: A real 4x price rise for Claude 3.5 Haiku, dated 2024. Anthropic tied it to greater intelligence in a new model, not to costs for comparable service, so it does not meet the support condition.

From June 2026, programmatic subscription use was billed at API rates, citing strain on flat-rate pricing. That is cost-related but narrow, affecting one group of users. It is not a broad price rise. Secondary source.
API rates were unchanged or falling and interactive plans were untouched. This shows the 2026 change was narrow. It is not evidence of sustained profitability, so it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet shows only a capability-justified new-model price rise and a narrow repricing of programmatic subscription use, while API prices held or fell. No broad, cost-driven price rise and no collapse is shown, so the early-support rule is not met. Profitability was not checked, so the early-contradiction rule is not met either. The outcome stays open.
